explanation: A parabola is every point that is equally far from a single focus point and a straight directrix line. The vertex (h, k) sits exactly halfway between them, and a controls how tightly the curve wraps the focus: the focal distance is 1/(4a), so a small a flings the focus far away and opens a wide bowl. Watch the orange point ride the curve — its green leg (to the focus) and orange leg (down to the directrix) stay equal length the whole way.
bullets: Vertex (h, k) is the turning point; the line x = h is the axis of symmetry.
Focus is 1/(4a) above the vertex; the directrix is the same distance below.
Defining property: every point is equidistant from the focus and the directrix.
